Source description explicitly identifies 枣阳九连墩二号墓出土虎座鸟架鼓. Commons categories include Collections of Hubei Provincial Museum and Jiuliandun Tombs.

Visual comparison with museum image /private/tmp/jingchu-assets/jiuliandun-tiger-bird-drum.jpeg: two outward-facing phoenixes with very long necks on outward-facing tigers; two smaller tigers support central circular drum; snakes beneath and between tiger seats; recognizable claw, eye, tail, wing and beak geometry agree. HOWEVER, the Commons photo shows a complete circular drum face and smooth outer drum shell in the exhibition, whereas the official white-background image shows only a broken circular frame. These are materially different display/conservation states. Do not imply the photos have the same central-drum condition; present the Commons photograph as a dated museum display photograph. Whether its complete drum component is restored or a replica has not been verified from an authoritative source.
